title: Production Quantization — AWQ, GPTQ, GGUF K-quants, FP8, MXFP4/NVFP4

questions.question: Which local format is singled out for serving one base model with many LoRA adapters in vLLM?
questions.explanation: The GPTQ-Int4 + Marlin row notes multi-LoRA support; the lesson uses that workload as GPTQ's distinctive production advantage.

questions.question: What is the approximate weight memory for a 70B model at INT4 in memory_breakdown?
questions.explanation: weight_gb is params_b * weight_bits / 8, so 70 × 4 / 8 = 35 GB before KV cache and activations.

questions.question: What happens to KV precision when the AWQ format is selected in FORMATS?
options: It automatically becomes 4 bits with the weights
It is removed from the memory calculation
It is always set to 32 bits
questions.explanation: AWQ-Int4 + Marlin has weight_bits=4 but kv_bits=16, so quantizing weights does not silently quantize the KV cache.

questions.question: Which format does the lesson position as the safer quality choice for reasoning-heavy workloads?
questions.explanation: The FP8 row is labeled safe default reasoning; aggressive FP4 formats require per-model validation because quality drops can show up on reasoning tasks.

questions.question: Why can a calibration set built from generic web text hurt a medical or code deployment?
options: Calibration changes the model's tokenizer vocabulary only
It increases KV precision to 32 bits
It makes all formats use the same engine
questions.explanation: AWQ/GPTQ calibration chooses quantization behavior from representative examples; a domain mismatch can degrade domain-specific accuracy.

questions.question: Why should a 4-bit weight result not be treated as the whole production memory budget?
options: The weight file is always larger than the model parameter count
KV and activations still scale with context/concurrency
Quantized weights cannot be loaded into HBM
The simulator ignores weight memory entirely
questions.explanation: memory_breakdown adds weight, KV, and activation terms; KV grows with concurrency × context and can consume the memory saved by weight quantization.
